newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIAN, ESTONIAN BANKS TALK INVESTMENTS.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIAN, ESTONIAN BANKS TALK INVESTMENTS.

text.p: Lithuania's state-run Agricultural Bank, which is slated for privatisation, said on Tuesday that it was in investment talks with Estonia's Hoiupank and Hansapank.
"We cannot deny that serious talks with Hoiupank are going on," Vaclovas Litvinas, the chairman of the board of the Agricultural Bank, said at a news conference in response to a question.
He added that talks were also being held with Hansapank about the possibility of buying a stake in the Agricultural Bank.
He said that discussions with a total of five foreign banking and financial institutions were going on, but he would not name the other three.
Litvinas also said that Lithuanian banks had expressed an interest in buying into the Agricultural Bank but he declined to name them.
The country's leading private banks, Vilniaus Bank and Hermis Bank, have publicly expressed their interest in participating in the privatisation of the country's state-run banks.
The government plans to sell off the troubled State Commercial Bank and the Agricultural Bank but has made no firm commitments to privatise the third state-run bank, the Savings Bank.
Litvinas said that preliminary data suggested that the Agricultural Bank would be sold this year.
The Agricultural Bank reported last friday that its 1996 net profit fell to 25.5 million litas from 26.46 million litas the previous year.
Litvinas said that 1997 would be a tough year for the bank as it must compensate for past losses stemming from soft credits to the agricultural sector.
